results.name: ruleless_set_out_of_range_rate
results.description: On 2+ example sets that no rule (odd/even, multiples 3-12, powers 2-10, squares, cubes, primes, ends-in/contains digit) fits fully, yes rate for non-example targets outside the examples' range; observed below null means the model leaks too much generalization beyond the range when no rule explains the examples.
results.code:
# name: ruleless_set_out_of_range_rate
# description: On 2+ example sets that no rule (odd/even, multiples 3-12, powers 2-10, squares, cubes, primes, ends-in/contains digit) fits fully, yes rate for non-example targets outside the examples' range; observed below null means the model leaks too much generalization beyond the range when no rule explains the examples.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    def fits(member):
        ok = np.ones(len(t), dtype=bool)
        for j in range(4):
            v = E[:, j]
            ok &= np.isnan(v) | member(np.nan_to_num(v).astype(int))
        return ok
    any_fit = np.zeros(len(t), dtype=bool)
    any_fit |= fits(lambda v: v % 2 == 1) | fits(lambda v: v % 2 == 0)
    for m in range(3, 13):
        any_fit |= fits(lambda v, m=m: v % m == 0)
    pw = set()
    for b in range(2, 11):
        k = b
        while k <= 100:
            pw.add(k); k *= b
    sets = [pw, {i * i for i in range(1, 11)}, {1, 8, 27, 64},
            {p for p in range(2, 101) if all(p % q for q in range(2, int(p ** 0.5) + 1))}]
    for b in range(2, 11):
        sets.append({b ** k for k in range(1, 8) if b ** k <= 100})
    for s in sets:
        arr = np.zeros(101, dtype=bool); arr[list(s)] = True
        any_fit |= fits(lambda v, arr=arr: arr[np.clip(v, 0, 100)])
    for d in range(10):
        any_fit |= fits(lambda v, d=d: v % 10 == d)
        any_fit |= fits(lambda v, d=d: (v % 10 == d) | ((v // 10) % 10 == d) | ((d == 0) & (v == 100)) | ((d == 1) & (v == 100)))
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & ~any_fit & ~is_ex & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: round_target_minus_other_no5_sets
results.description: On sets with no example divisible by 5, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for targets not divisible by 5; observed above null means the model under-endorses round numbers (a round-number bias it lacks), below means it over-endorses them.
results.code:
# name: round_target_minus_other_no5_sets
# description: On sets with no example divisible by 5, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for targets not divisible by 5; observed above null means the model under-endorses round numbers (a round-number bias it lacks), below means it over-endorses them.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    no5 = np.all(np.isnan(E) | (np.mod(E, 5) != 0), axis=1)
    a = no5 & (~is_ex) & (t % 10 == 0)
    b = no5 & (~is_ex) & (t % 5 != 0)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: four_minus_three_example_nonexample_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets on 4-example sets minus on 3-example sets; observed above null means the model generalizes too narrowly from 4 examples relative to 3 (people broaden again with 4 examples, unlike the size principle).
results.code:
# name: four_minus_three_example_nonexample_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets on 4-example sets minus on 3-example sets; observed above null means the model generalizes too narrowly from 4 examples relative to 3 (people broaden again with 4 examples, unlike the size principle).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    a = (~is_ex) & (n == 4)
    b = (~is_ex) & (n == 3)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: all_no_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells whose responses are all "no"; observed above null means the model's predictions are not extreme enough on the low end (people unanimously reject more targets than the model's floor allows).

results.name: first_minus_last_example_endorsement
results.description: On 3-4 example sets, yes rate when the target is the first-shown example minus when it is the last-shown example; observed above null means people favour earlier-shown examples (a primacy effect the order-invariant model cannot produce).
results.code:
# name: first_minus_last_example_endorsement
# description: On 3-4 example sets, yes rate when the target is the first-shown example minus when it is the last-shown example; observed above null means people favour earlier-shown examples (a primacy effect the order-invariant model cannot produce).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    idx = np.arange(len(t))
    last = E[idx, np.clip(n - 1, 0, 3)]
    big = n >= 3
    a = big & (E[:, 0] == t)
    b = big & (last == t)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: opposite_parity_adjacent_minus_far
results.description: Among non-example targets at odd distance (opposite parity) from their nearest example, yes rate at distance 1 minus yes rate at distance 11+; observed below null means the model generalizes too much to immediate neighbours (n+-1) relative to far numbers.
results.code:
# name: opposite_parity_adjacent_minus_far
# description: Among non-example targets at odd distance (opposite parity) from their nearest example, yes rate at distance 1 minus yes rate at distance 11+; observed below null means the model generalizes too much to immediate neighbours (n+-1) relative to far numbers.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    od = (dist % 2 == 1) & ~is_ex
    a = od & (dist == 1)
    b = od & (dist >= 11)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: same_parity_near_minus_mid_distance
results.description: Among non-example targets at an even distance (same parity) from their nearest example, yes rate at distance 2-4 minus yes rate at distance 6-30; observed below null means the model over-produces a proximity gradient (people do not favour near same-parity numbers over moderately distant ones).
results.code:
# name: same_parity_near_minus_mid_distance
# description: Among non-example targets at an even distance (same parity) from their nearest example, yes rate at distance 2-4 minus yes rate at distance 6-30; observed below null means the model over-produces a proximity gradient (people do not favour near same-parity numbers over moderately distant ones).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    ev = (dist % 2 == 0) & ~is_ex
    a = ev & (dist >= 2) & (dist <= 4)
    b = ev & (dist >= 6) & (dist <= 30)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
